titulo: Practical versus Theoretical Teaching of Abnormal Physical Examination Findings to Medical Students: A Randomized Controlled Trial
tituloEs: La práctica con simuladores mejora el aprendizaje del examen físico patológico en estudiantes
revista: Advances in medical education and practice
resumenOriginal:
Introduction: Approximately 10% of diagnostic errors can be attributed to the physical examination portion of a clinical workup. Physical examination skills among medical students are deficient but what is deficient in the students' ability to examine is unclear. Teaching physical examination using task-trainers has been viewed positively but medical programs often lack dedicated task-trainer sessions for teaching abnormal physical examination. We hypothesize that teaching abnormal findings practically is better than teaching them theoretically.

Methods: The study had two sections: survey and task-trainer sections. The survey was distributed to all medical college students. Many students proceeded to the task trainer section where they were randomized 1:1 to either a control (theoretical abnormal) or experimental (practical abnormal) session that covered cardiopulmonary physical examination. Task-trainer students performed pre- and post-intervention quizzes, an OSCE-style final evaluation, and a final survey.

Results: Students overwhelmingly had positive comments regarding the session and suggested integrating them in preclinical years. Experimental arm students passed the OSCE-style evaluation at a significantly higher rate than control students (68.3% vs 33.3%, respectively). There is no statistically significant change in pre-post quiz scores between arms.

Conclusions: Compared to theoretically teaching abnormal findings, task trainer-based abnormal physical examination teaching increases the students' technique quality, ability to elicit findings, reasoning, and ability to diagnose correctly.

tips.texto: Incorporar sesiones con simuladores de hallazgos anormales desde los años preclínicos, no solo en etapas tardías del currículo.
El conocimiento teórico solo no mejora el rendimiento. Enfocarse en práctica deliberada de la técnica de exploración.
Usar estaciones OSCE que evalúen no solo hallazgos sino calidad de técnica y razonamiento diagnóstico integrado.
No asumir que los estudiantes aprenden hallazgos patológicos solo viendo casos normales; enseñarlos explícitamente.
Iniciar con sistemas cardiopulmonar donde los simuladores permiten reproducir hallazgos críticos de manera confiable.

sintesis: Este ensayo aleatorizado comparó la enseñanza teórica versus práctica (con simuladores) de hallazgos anormales en examen cardiopulmonar. Los estudiantes que practicaron con simuladores aprobaron la evaluación OSCE a tasas significativamente mayores (68.3% vs 33.3%).
aplicacionDocente: Solicitar tiempo con simuladores de hallazgos patológicos antes de las rotaciones clínicas. En la práctica, dedicar la primera exploración supervisada a técnica, no solo a identificar signos. Rediseñar evaluaciones para incluir ejecución de maniobras, no únicamente interpretación de casos escritos.
disenoEstudio: Ensayo controlado aleatorizado en estudiantes de medicina de pregrado
fraseInfografia: Practicar hallazgos anormales con simuladores duplica la tasa de aprobación en OSCE
advertencia: El estudio no reporta tamaño muestral ni seguimiento a largo plazo de retención de habilidades.
